scaleNote: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, 2026 rebased scale (top models ~ 55-63). Snapshots: August 30, 2026 (BenchLM mirror) for the top ten, August 27, 2026 (ModelCap mirror) for the rest; retrieved August 31, 2026. August scores sit roughly 1.5 to 2.5 points above July across the whole table, so treat month-to-month differences as a shift in the index, not as every model improving at once.
specNote: Context, price and release data come from vendor pages and public pricing mirrors (retrieved August 31, 2026). Missing values are not published or not yet verified - shown as -.

models.name: GPT-6
models.access: Not announced - no confirmed date or specs
models.review: OpenAI's expected next-numbered flagship: reports point to deeper reasoning, multimodality and agentic tool use, likely in several tiers. Everything about it - including the name - is rumor until OpenAI speaks.

models.name: GPT-5.6 Sol
models.access: Released July 9, 2026 (rolling out) · API $5/$30 per 1M tokens · up to 750 tok/s on Cerebras
models.review: OpenAI's new flagship and #1 on the public AA index snapshot: max reasoning effort, programmatic tool calling, and an 'ultra mode' that spins up subagents. The model to beat for hard reasoning and agentic work.

models.name: GPT-5.6 Terra
models.review: The balanced tier of the GPT-5.6 family - GPT-5.5-level quality at half the price. On track to become the everyday ChatGPT default.

models.name: GPT-5.6 Luna
models.review: The fast, affordable member of the 5.6 series - near-flagship scores at commodity prices; strong default for high-volume API work.

models.name: GPT-5.5
models.review: The April 2026 flagship, still the strongest broad generalist most people can use free: brainstorming, drafting, frontier coding (SWE-bench Verified 88.7%).

models.name: GPT-5.5 Pro
models.review: Maximum-reasoning tier of GPT-5.5 - statistically tied with the very top on many boards. Overkill for everyday tasks.

models.name: GPT-5.4
models.access: ChatGPT Plus · API · inside Perplexity Pro
models.review: The previous flagship, still very strong and a reliable known quantity - often cheaper per token than its successors.

models.name: GPT-5.4 mini
models.access: API (cheap tier) · serves ChatGPT free-tier overflow
models.review: Small, quick, cheap - the sensible default for classification, extraction and light drafting at volume.

models.name: GPT-5.4 nano
models.review: OpenAI's smallest current model - surprisingly capable for its price class, built for massive-scale simple tasks.

models.name: GPT-5.3-Codex
models.review: Coding specialist built for agentic dev workflows rather than chat - punches far above its overall index score inside a code editor.

models.name: GPT-5.2
models.review: Early-2026 default, now superseded - fine for light tasks, noticeably weaker on hard reasoning.

models.name: GPT-5.1
models.review: Late-2025 generation, kept for compatibility - two clear steps behind the current line.

models.name: GPT-5
models.review: The model that unified the GPT-4/o-series era in August 2025. Historically important; superseded several times since.

models.name: o3-pro
models.review: The 2025 deep-reasoning specialist - slow and dated now, but a milestone in chain-of-thought models.

models.name: o3
models.review: Once the reasoning benchmark-setter; today mainly of historical and compatibility interest.

models.name: GPT-4.1
models.review: 2025 workhorse with a then-notable 1M context. Cheap, stable, far from frontier.

models.name: GPT-4o
models.review: The 2024-25 multimodal workhorse. Historically important, no longer competitive on quality - kept for compatibility.

models.name: gpt-oss-120b
models.review: OpenAI's open-weight release - modest by 2026 standards but fully downloadable and permissively licensed.

models.name: gpt-oss-20b
models.access: Open weights · runs on a laptop
models.review: The small sibling - one of the easiest capable models to run fully offline on consumer hardware.

models.name: Claude Opus 5
models.access: Released July 24, 2026 · Claude Pro / Max plans · API $5/$25 per 1M tokens (Fast mode $10/$50)
models.review: Anthropic's fourth release in two months and the new overall #1: tops the AA Intelligence Index (60.7) and the Agentic Index (55.3) with 1M context, default thinking and computer use, at unchanged Opus pricing. Near-Fable quality at half the price.

models.name: Claude Mythos 5
models.access: Approved organizations only (Project Glasswing); US government-cleared, expanding
models.review: Same underlying model as Fable 5 with dual-use safeguards lifted for vetted organizations; deployed on critical infrastructure in 15+ countries.

models.name: Claude Fable 5
models.access: Claude Pro / Max plans (usage credits since July 7) · API $10/$50 per 1M tokens
models.review: Anthropic's newest flagship (Mythos-class) - tops the AA index at max effort and leads creative-writing boards for voice, subtext and character work; briefly export-controlled, now globally available.

models.name: Claude Opus 4.8
models.review: #2 on the public AA snapshot and the leader in real-repo coding (SWE-bench Pro 69.2%). For serious software work, still the default answer.

models.name: Claude Opus 4.7
models.review: Still top-10 with adaptive reasoning - a capable fallback where 4.8 isn't available.

models.name: Claude Sonnet 5

spec.note: the $2/$10 introductory API price expired Aug 31, 2026

models.review: The strongest free option on the market - frontier-adjacent writing and coding quality at zero cost. Best zero-budget daily driver for text work.

models.name: Claude Sonnet 4.6
models.review: The previous balanced default of the Claude line - solid quality at higher limits and lower cost.

models.name: Claude Haiku 4.5
models.access: All Claude tiers · cheapest Claude via API
models.review: Fastest and cheapest of the line - quick answers, classification, high-volume light tasks.

models.name: Claude Opus 4.6
models.review: Early-2026 Opus, superseded twice since - retained mainly for pinned enterprise workflows.

models.name: Claude Opus 4.5
models.review: The late-2025 flagship that made agentic coding mainstream; now two generations back.

models.name: Claude Opus 4.1
models.review: Mid-2025 generation - of historical interest and for compatibility with older pipelines.

models.name: Claude 3 Opus
models.review: The 2024 model that first made Claude famous for prose quality. Retired from frontier duty.

models.name: Gemini 3 Ultra
models.access: Reported as upcoming - no official availability
models.review: Reported top tier above Gemini 3.1 Pro with wider API access said to be coming; Google has published nothing definitive - treat specs as rumor.

models.name: Gemini 3.1 Pro
models.access: Google AI Pro $19.99/mo · API · inside Perplexity Pro
models.review: #1 in LMArena's coding arena at launch, deep Google Workspace integration and strong multimodal work.

models.name: Gemini 3.5 Pro
models.access: Not announced. Release-timing reports around the Kimi K3 launch called it imminent; nothing official from Google
models.review: The widely expected Pro refresh of the Gemini line. Third-party release trackers treated it as imminent in late July; until Google speaks, everything here (including the name) is rumor and the score is a placeholder estimate.

models.name: Gemini 3.7 Flash

spec.note: introductory price to Dec 31, 2026 - then $1.50/$7.50 · 64K max output

models.access: Released August 13, 2026 · API $0.75/$3.75 per 1M tokens (introductory, doubles Jan 1, 2027) · model id gemini-3.7-flash · free-tier availability not confirmed
models.review: Google's August workhorse, aimed squarely at coding and agents: 85.8% on Terminal-bench 2.1, 97.0% on long-context recall at 128K, and half the price of 3.6 Flash until the end of the year. WhichAI still defaults auto-run to gemini-3.6-flash because that model's free tier is confirmed and this one's is not - switch it in Settings if Google has enabled yours.

models.name: Gemini 3.6 Flash
models.access: Free tier in AI Studio and the Gemini app (rate-limited) · API $1.50/$7.50 per 1M tokens
models.review: Google's July refresh of the free workhorse: 3.5 Flash quality with cheaper output ($7.50 vs $9), 1M context, day one in AI Studio, the API and the app. The new default of the Gemini line.

models.name: Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite
models.review: The routing tier of the July refresh: classification, extraction, tagging and short summaries at commodity prices. Not built for hard reasoning.

models.name: Gemini 3.5 Flash
models.access: FREE (most generous free tier) · free API via Google AI Studio
models.review: Remarkable: the newest Flash now outscores the older 3.1 Pro on the AA index - frontier-adjacent quality, free, and the model WhichAI auto-runs with your AI Studio key.

models.name: Gemini 3 Pro
models.review: Previous Pro generation, still widely deployed across Google products.

models.name: Gemini 3 Flash
models.review: The earlier fast tier - inexpensive and quick, now clearly behind 3.5 Flash.

models.name: Gemini 3.1 Flash-Lite
models.access: Free API (highest free rate limits: 15 RPM, 1,000/day)
models.review: The volume workhorse: the most generous free API quota of any capable model.

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Pro
models.review: The 2025 flagship, superseded by the Gemini 3 line.

models.name: Gemini 2.5 Flash
models.review: 2025's fast tier, kept for compatibility.

models.name: Gemma 4 31B
models.access: Open weights · runs on consumer hardware
models.review: Google's open family - one of the best models you can run locally on a single GPU.

models.name: Gemma 4 12B
models.review: The mid-size Gemma - a favorite for private, offline use on ordinary hardware.

models.name: Gemma 3 27B
models.review: The 2025 open generation, superseded by Gemma 4.

models.name: Grok 5
models.access: Not released - repeatedly delayed (prediction markets price a near-term launch low)
models.review: xAI's long-promised next flagship. Timelines have slipped more than once; any spec you read is speculation.

models.name: Grok 4.6

spec.note: $0.50 per 1M cached input · reasoning effort: low / medium / high / xhigh

models.access: Released August 12, 2026 · API $2/$6 per 1M tokens ($0.50 cached) · in Grok Build and Cursor · SuperGrok subscription
models.review: xAI's August flagship and its first entry in the AA top three (60.9): 70.8% on CursorBench 3.2, 87.0% on VulcanBench v3, and selectable reasoning effort from low to xhigh. Two honest caveats: the 500K context is half what the Claude, GPT and Kimi flagships offer, and measured throughput (~58 tok/s) sits below the field median.

models.name: Grok 4.5
models.access: Released July 8, 2026 · API $2/$6 per 1M tokens · in Grok Build & Cursor · not yet in the EU
models.review: xAI's first model built specifically for coding and agents (1.5T-parameter base, trained on real Cursor sessions): #4 on the AA index at a fraction of flagship prices. EU availability pending.

models.name: Grok 4.1
models.access: Free tier on X / grok.com · paid from ~$16/mo · API
models.review: Direct, up-to-the-minute answers with X data, a Think mode and a 2M-token context; among the lowest measured hallucination rates (~4%).

models.name: Grok 4.3
models.review: Spring-2026 generation - a solid step over Grok 4.1 on reasoning, now overshadowed by 4.5.

models.name: Grok Build 0.1
models.review: The agent-tuned model behind xAI's Grok Build environment - sessions, skills, plugins and repo-scale work rather than chat.

models.name: Grok Code Fast 1
models.access: API (very cheap) · common inside IDE integrations
models.review: Tiny, fast coding model - autocompletion-class work at near-zero cost, not for hard problems.

models.name: Grok 4
models.review: Previous xAI generation - superseded by 4.1's larger context and then by the 4.3/4.5 wave.

models.name: Llama 5
models.access: Not announced - no weights, no model card
models.review: Persistent rumors, zero official signal: no Meta announcement and no Hugging Face weights. Any 'Llama 5 review' online is premature or invented. Meta's proprietary Muse line now gets the frontier attention.

models.name: Muse Spark 1.2
models.access: API via Meta Superintelligence Labs (August 6, 2026 refresh of the 1.1 line)
models.review: Meta's August refresh puts the Muse line back in the top ten (56.8, up 3.6 from 1.1): the strongest showing yet for Meta's proprietary track, and a reminder that the Llama brand is no longer where Meta's frontier work happens.

models.name: Muse Spark 1.1
models.access: API via Meta Superintelligence Labs (Meta's first paid model, July 9, 2026)
models.review: Meta's first proprietary, paid model line (Meta Superintelligence Labs): natively multimodal reasoning with visual chain-of-thought and multi-agent orchestration. A strategic U-turn from open weights.

models.name: Meta AI
models.access: FREE - meta.ai and inside WhatsApp, Instagram, Messenger
models.review: Not a model but an assistant woven into Meta's apps, now increasingly powered by the Muse line with real-time info via search. Ubiquitous and free.

models.name: Llama 4 Maverick
models.access: Open weights · FREE fast inference on Groq
models.review: The larger Llama 4 - near-instant on Groq and fine for drafts, but the index is honest: it sits far below the 2026 open leaders.

models.name: Llama 4 Scout
models.review: Llama 4's efficient sibling with an enormous context window - useful locally, weak on hard tasks.

models.name: Llama 3.3 70B
models.access: Open weights · FREE on Groq (WhichAI default runner)
models.review: Older but dependable - the default model WhichAI auto-runs with a free Groq key.

models.name: Llama 3.1 405B
models.review: 2024's open giant - a milestone for open AI, now outclassed by far smaller models.

models.name: Copilot (GPT-5 family)
models.access: Free tier · Copilot Pro $20/mo · built into Windows & Microsoft 365
models.review: Not a model but a delivery vehicle: OpenAI GPT-5-family models woven into Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams and Windows.

models.name: Phi-4
models.review: Microsoft's small open research line - historically interesting for data-quality tricks, no longer competitive.

models.name: Perplexity Sonar
models.access: FREE: unlimited basic cited searches + 5 Pro searches/day
models.review: Search-answer engine rather than a chat model: best-in-class citation accuracy - a smarter, cited replacement for googling.

models.name: Perplexity Sonar Pro + Deep Research
models.access: Perplexity Pro $20/mo (includes GPT, Claude and Gemini flagships inside)
models.review: Deeper retrieval, 20 Deep Research runs/day, and frontier models selectable inside one subscription.

models.name: DeepSeek V4 Pro
models.access: Free chat app · open weights · very cheap API · 1M context default
models.review: The open reasoning champion (1.6T sparse MoE, 49B active): tops open coding boards at famously low prices - the most popular frontier-adjacent free model worldwide.

models.name: DeepSeek V4 Flash
models.access: Free chat app · open weights · cheapest DeepSeek API
models.review: The efficient V4 (284B total, 13B active) - most of Pro's quality at a fraction of the compute.

models.name: DeepSeek V3.2
models.review: The 2025 generation that made ultra-cheap frontier-adjacent AI mainstream; superseded by V4.

models.name: DeepSeek R1
models.review: The January 2025 release that shocked the market by open-sourcing o1-class reasoning. Historic; superseded.

models.name: Qwen3.8 Max (preview)
models.access: Early preview via Qwen chat and Alibaba Cloud (July 19) · specs not final
models.review: Alibaba's next flagship in early preview. No published index score yet; expect it above Qwen3.7 Max (46.0) once measured. Everything here is provisional.

models.name: Qwen3.7 Max
models.access: Free chat app · API (closed weights for Max tier)
models.review: Alibaba's strongest current model and the top Chinese closed-weights entry on the AA index - outstanding multilingual coverage.

models.name: Qwen3.7 Plus
models.review: The balanced tier of the 3.7 line - strong value for multilingual work at volume.

models.name: Qwen3.6 Plus
models.access: Free chat app · open-weight siblings · API
models.review: Among the strongest open lines for coding and clearly the best multilingual open family.

models.name: Qwen3.6-27B
models.access: Open weights (Apache 2.0) · runs on a good desktop
models.review: Possibly the best quality-per-GB you can download today - near mid-frontier scores from a 27B you can run yourself.

models.name: Qwen3.5 397B
models.review: The open MoE flagship of the 3.5 wave - big, capable, Apache-licensed.

models.name: Qwen3 Coder
models.access: Open weights · FREE on OpenRouter (qwen/qwen3-coder:free, 1M context) - WhichAI auto-runs it with a free OpenRouter key
models.review: The strongest free coding route on OpenRouter right now - 1M context, tool use, zero cost within the daily free limits.

models.name: Kimi K3
models.access: API $3/$15 per 1M tokens ($0.30 cached) · free kimi.com chat · open weights on Hugging Face (July 27, Modified MIT)
models.review: Moonshot's July 16 flagship: 2.8T-parameter MoE with 1M context and native vision. #3 on the AA index (57.1), best published BrowseComp (91.2%) and #1 Frontend Code Arena at launch - the strongest agentic challenger to the US frontier.

models.name: Kimi K2.6
models.access: Open weights · API hosts · free chat app
models.review: Strong open coding (SWE-bench Verified 80.2%) and long agentic tasks - now the smaller sibling of the flagship K3.

models.name: Kimi K2.7 Code
models.access: Early access via Moonshot · open weights promised
models.review: Moonshot's agentic-coding bet - early numbers put it just behind K2.6 overall but ahead on real-repo work.

models.name: Kimi K2.5
models.review: The previous Kimi - still a solid open all-rounder with excellent long-context behavior.

models.name: GLM-5.3

spec.note: 743B post-trained base · weights held back pending a staged safety review · price not published

models.access: Released August 14, 2026 · staged access · open weights NOT released at launch (unlike every previous GLM) · API price not published
models.review: Z.ai's 743B flagship: AA 59.5, the highest a Chinese lab has scored, with 84.5% on CyberGym and 54.4% on ExploitBench. The break with tradition matters more than the score: weights are held back behind a staged safety review, so for now GLM-5.3 is not the open model its version number suggests. The Flash sibling is.

models.name: GLM-5.3-Flash
models.access: Released August 26, 2026 · open weights under MIT · API $0.15/$0.50 per 1M tokens · free chat at chat.z.ai
models.review: The most capable freely downloadable model on this table: 320B-A18B, MIT licence, 1M multimodal context, and $0.15/$0.50 hosted - roughly a thirtieth of what the frontier charges for a score within six points of it. If one entry explains why the open-weight gap stopped mattering in 2026, it is this one.

models.name: GLM-5.2
models.review: The strongest open-weight model in the world right now (#10 overall, above Gemini 3.1 Pro): SWE-bench Pro 62.1%, #2 React on Code Arena - frontier coding at open prices.

models.name: GLM-5.1
models.review: The previous Z.ai release - still strong, quickly superseded by 5.2.

models.name: GLM-5
models.review: The early-2026 base of the GLM-5 family that put Z.ai on the frontier map.

models.name: Hunyuan 3.0 (Hy3)
models.access: Open weights (Apache 2.0, released July 6, 2026) · 295B MoE, 21B active · 256K context
models.review: Tencent's move into the open-weight camp - one of the last big closed Chinese labs to open up, days ago. Solid mid-frontier scores and a permissive license.

models.name: Doubao Seed 2.1 Pro
models.access: China-focused: served via ByteDance's Volcano Engine cloud only
models.review: Built for raw scale - the Doubao family reportedly handles over a hundred trillion token calls a day, mostly inside China's consumer apps. Hard to access from the West.

models.name: ERNIE 5.1
models.review: Baidu's flagship stays closed and China-centric - competitive domestically, rarely benchmarked on Western boards.

models.name: MiMo-V2.5-Pro
models.review: Xiaomi's surprisingly strong in-house line (an Omni sibling handles voice/vision on-device) - a sign of how deep the Chinese frontier bench now runs.

models.name: Ling 2.6 Flash
models.review: Ant Group's efficient open line - built for cheap, fast serving rather than peak intelligence.

models.name: Step 3.7 Flash
models.review: StepFun's fast open tier - part of the broad Chinese open-weight wave now taking ~45% of OpenRouter traffic.

models.name: MiniMax M3
models.review: MiniMax's new flagship - #2 open model on the index behind GLM-5.2, with a reputation for huge context handling.

models.name: MiniMax M2.7
models.review: Strong open coding contender in head-to-head arenas - less known in the West, worth watching.

models.name: Inkling
models.access: Open weights (Apache 2.0) on Hugging Face · Tinker API (256K ctx)
models.review: Thinking Machines' first open release: 975B-parameter MoE (41B active) reasoning natively over text, images and audio, with controllable thinking effort - the new leading US open-weights base for customization.

models.name: Nemotron 3 Ultra
models.access: FREE on OpenRouter (nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b:free - WhichAI default runner) · open weights · Perplexity Pro
models.review: Strongest US open model and extremely fast (400+ tokens/second on some hosts) - and genuinely free via OpenRouter.

models.name: Nemotron 3 Super
models.review: The 120B sibling - lighter, faster, still free; good for volume tasks.

models.name: Mistral Medium 3.5
models.review: Mistral's current best on the index - a newer generation that outscores the bigger, older Large 3. Europe's leading open lab.

models.name: Mistral Large 3
models.access: Open weights · Le Chat free tier · API
models.review: The 675B MoE that was Europe's flagship in 2025 - the index now places it well behind newer, smaller Mistral releases.

models.name: Mistral Small 4
models.review: Compact European open model - a common pick for private, on-premise deployments.

models.name: Ministral 3 14B
models.review: Mistral's edge line - built to run on phones and small boxes, not to win benchmarks.

models.name: Mercury 2
models.review: A diffusion language model - generates text in parallel rather than token-by-token, hitting extreme speeds. The most interesting architectural outsider on the board.

models.name: Command A+
models.access: Enterprise API · open weights for research · private deployments
models.review: Enterprise-focused: retrieval-augmented answers, data residency, private deployment - chosen for compliance more than raw benchmarks.

models.name: Nova 2
models.review: Amazon's in-house line, priced aggressively inside Bedrock - the default for AWS-native companies, not a benchmark leader.

models.name: Granite 4.0
models.review: IBM's open enterprise family (hybrid Mamba architecture, tiny-to-mid sizes) - built for governed, on-premise business use, not leaderboards.

models.name: Jamba Large
models.review: AI21's hybrid SSM-Transformer line - memory-efficient very-long-context processing for enterprises, a different trade-off than pure Transformers.

models.name: K-Exaone
models.access: Korean cloud ecosystem · some open releases
models.review: Korea's leading domestic line - strong on Korean-language benchmarks, part of the sovereign-AI wave.

models.name: Solar Pro 2
models.review: Upstage's efficient Korean-market model - document AI and enterprise Korean text are its home turf.

models.name: Trinity Large
models.review: A rare US startup training capable open models from scratch - the 'Trinity' line is the credible American answer to the Chinese open wave.

models.name: Sarvam 105B
models.review: India's sovereign-AI flagship - optimized for Indic languages, a milestone for AI outside the US-China duopoly.

models.name: Falcon H1
models.review: The UAE's hybrid-architecture open family - a persistent, well-funded outsider rather than a frontier contender.

models.name: Reka Flash 3
models.review: Small multimodal open model from an ex-DeepMind team - efficient vision-language work on modest hardware.

models.name: OLMo 2
models.access: Fully open: weights, data and training code
models.review: The most transparent model line in existence - everything is published, including training data. Built for science, not benchmarks.

models.name: LFM2.5
models.review: 'Liquid' non-Transformer architecture squeezing real capability into phone-sized models - watch this space for on-device AI.
